div.p: Catachan is a Death World. A planet where every plant, every animal, every breath of air wants you dead. There is no gold here. No glory. Only survival. The jungle doesn't care about your rank, your medals, or your prayers to the God-Emperor. It only cares that you are meat, and meat is food.

You are Catachan Jungle Fighters. Born and raised on this hell-world, you've survived where millions have died. You've learned to read the signs—the way the leaves rustle when something big is hunting, the smell of death on the wind, the silence that means something is watching. You've learned that the jungle is always hungry, always waiting, always ready to kill.

This isn't a war against enemies you can see. This is survival against a planet that wants you dead. Every step could be your last. That vine? It might strangle you. That flower? Its pollen might dissolve your lungs. That shadow? It might be a Catachan Devil, and you're already dead. But you're Catachan. You've survived this long. The jungle hasn't killed you yet, and it won't kill you today.

You and your squad are those survivors. You go where the jungle is thickest, where the danger is greatest, where missions take you deep into the heart of death itself. There are monstrous things lurking in every shadow. Are you ready to face them?

You move like a ghost through the jungle. While the others crash through the undergrowth like grox in a china shop, you're already ahead, reading the signs, spotting the ambushes before they happen. You've spent more time alone in the deep jungle than most men have spent breathing. You know which plants will kill you, which animals are hunting, and which shadows are just shadows.

Your squad relies on you. Without your eyes, they'd walk into a Catachan Devil's nest. Without your ears, they'd miss the sound of something big moving in the canopy. Without your instincts, they'd all be dead. You're the one who finds the safe paths, the clean water, the high ground. You're the one who keeps them alive.
Keep moving. Keep watching. The jungle never sleeps.

On Catachan, death comes in a thousand forms. Poison. Disease. Wounds that won't heal. You've seen men die from scratches. You've seen men survive wounds that should have killed them instantly. You know which plants can save a life and which will end it. You know how to treat a man who's been stung by a death-spider, bitten by a venom-snake, or infected with jungle rot.

Your squad trusts you with their lives. Literally. When they're bleeding out, when the poison is spreading, when the fever is burning them alive, you're the one who saves them. You're the one who keeps them fighting when their bodies want to give up. You're the difference between life and death.
Save who you can. Learn from the ones you can't. The jungle teaches harsh lessons.

You've been fighting on Catachan longer than most of your squad has been alive. You've seen it all. The ambushes. The traps. The things that come out of the dark. You've lost more friends than you can count. You've got more scars than you have clean skin. And you're still here.

Experience is the only teacher that matters on a Death World. You've learned the hard way what works and what gets you killed. Your squad looks to you for wisdom, for leadership, for the knowledge that only comes from surviving when you shouldn't have. You've forgotten more about jungle warfare than most men will ever learn.
Pass on what you know. Keep them alive. That's your duty now.

You know which plants can save a life and which will end it. You know how to treat a man who's been stung by a death-spider, bitten by a venom-snake, or infected with jungle rot.

Your squad trusts you with their lives. Literally. When they're bleeding out, when the poison is spreading, when the fever is burning them alive, you're the one who saves them. You're the one who keeps them fighting when their bodies want to give up. You're the difference between life and death.
Save who you can. Learn from the ones you can't. The jungle teaches harsh lessons.

You kill from the shadows. One shot. One kill. That's your way. While the others are fighting in the open, you're in the canopy, in the rocks, in the perfect position. You've learned to wait. To watch. To strike when the moment is right. You've learned that the best way to survive is to never be seen at all.

Your lascarbine is an extension of your will. You know every creak, every whisper, every way it can kill. You've learned to read the wind, the light, the distance. You've learned to kill things that most men can't even see. You're the ghost in the jungle, the death that comes from nowhere.
Take the shot. Make it count. The jungle is watching.

Your chainsword is your best friend. You've killed more things with it than you have with your lasgun. When the fighting gets close, when the jungle closes in, when there's no room to shoot, that's when you shine. You've learned to fight in the dark, in the mud, in places where most men would die.

You're not afraid of close combat. You welcome it. You've learned that sometimes the best way to kill something is to get close enough to smell its breath. You've learned that a chainsword in the right place can kill things that bullets can't. You're the one who charges when others retreat, who fights when others run.
Get close. Get bloody. The jungle respects strength.

The jungle hates technology. The humidity rusts metal. The plants grow over machinery. The animals chew through cables. But you understand the machine-spirit. You know how to keep the weapons working when they shouldn't. You know how to repair the vox when it breaks. You know how to make the equipment last longer than it has any right to.

Your squad depends on their gear. Their lasguns. Their vox units. Their auspex scanners. When it breaks, when it fails, when the jungle tries to destroy it, you're the one who fixes it. You're the one who keeps the machine-spirit happy. You're the one who makes sure the technology survives the Death World.
Maintain the gear. Honor the machine-spirit. The jungle is always trying to break things.

Story.p: First, to see the characters survive the impossible. To see them face down creatures that shouldn't exist, navigate terrain that wants them dead, and complete missions that would kill lesser soldiers. To see them caught up in the constant struggle between man and a planet that wants to devour them.

Second, to see them rely on each other. To watch a squad work together despite their differences, to see them cover each other's backs when the jungle attacks, to witness the bonds forged in the crucible of constant danger. A Catachan squad that doesn't trust each other is a dead squad.

Third, because Catachan is endless. There are always new threats, new missions, new parts of the jungle that haven't been explored. The planet itself is the enemy, and it has plans of its own. Play to see what horrors await in the next clearing, what missions command will send you on, and how the jungle will try to kill you next.

This book will teach you how to play Deathworld. If you're going to be the GM, you'll need to read the whole thing, though you can skim through the monster stats for now and save the Advanced Missions chapter for later. Try printing the play aids too, they'll help you see what's most important. If you're a player, you might not need to read more than Playing the Game—a lot of the rules in Deathworld will be contained in the character sheets you use during the game itself. You'll come back to the text a few times throughout your game to refer to certain rules, but it should be a rare occasion.

To play Deathworld, you'll need to gather yourself and 2–5 friends. A group of 4 to 6, including you, is best. Choose one person to be the Game Master (GM). Everyone else will be players, taking the role of the characters in the game (we call these the player characters or PCs). As you play, the players say what their characters say, think, and do. The GM describes everything else in the world—especially the jungle and all the ways it wants to kill you.

You can play a single session or string together multiple sessions into a campaign. Plan accordingly if you plan on playing a campaign, maybe setting aside a night of the week to play. Each session will usually be a few hours and you'll be able to start playing right away within the first session.
You'll need to print some materials. Before you start a new game, find or print off at least:

ul.li: A few copies of the basic and special moves
One copy of each class sheet
One copy of the mission sheet and GM moves
Miscellanea such as: pens and pencils, scrap paper for maps and notes, maybe some index cards

Story.p: Everyone at the table will need something to write with and some six-sided dice. Two dice is the minimum but two dice per player is a good idea.
You'll also need some specialized dice: four-sided, eight-sided, ten-sided and twelve-sided. One of each is enough but more is better: you won't have to pass them around so much.

Playing Deathworld is all about finding out what happens when your squad of Catachan Jungle Fighters encounters the horrors of their homeworld, completes dangerous missions, and tries to survive another day on a planet that wants them dead. It's a conversation between the players and the GM—the GM tells the players what they see and hear in the jungle around them and the players say what their characters are thinking, feeling, and doing. Sometimes those descriptions will trigger a move—something that'll cause everyone to stop and say "time to roll the dice to see what happens." For a moment everyone hangs on the edges of their seats as the dice clatter to a stop. Tension and horror are always the result, no matter how the dice land.

As you play your characters they'll change from their missions and gain experience while learning about the jungle, overcoming threats, and surviving encounters that should have killed them. You'll discover how they feel about each other and how they cope with the constant pressure of a Death World. When they accrue enough experience they'll gain levels, becoming more skilled and having more options to survive.

You can play Deathworld with the same group, session to session, over a long series of missions, watching your characters change and grow together. You can play it as a self-contained game in a single-session, too. Whether a long campaign or a one-shot, Deathworld's rules are here to guide you and help you create a world of action and horror. Time to get out there and survive!
